primary_intervention_vector: GC-increased minus GC-decreased Layer-1 MLP representation
main_supported_claim: The GC-responsive Layer-1 MLP change contains a dominant low-dimensional direction strongly aligned with promoter representation. This direction generalizes to held-out sequences and preserves nearly all of the mean promoter-aligned GC shift. A small set of low-rank coordinates predicts a substantial portion of the downstream Layer-5 diagnostic-probe effect.
claim_boundary: Low-rank prediction and alignment do not establish causal mediation through the identified subspace.
The downstream target is a fixed diagnostic probe, not a native promoter-classification output of DNABERT-2.
The dominant shared GC direction is low-rank, but centered sequence-specific residuals are substantially more distributed.
GC-changing substitutions also alter local sequence context, motifs, dinucleotides, and tokenization.
